description: Toy Box Friends G2-14 (grade 2): needs (food, water, shelter, clothing) and wants, goods and services (the Basket Test), and choosing needs first when there are not enough tokens for everything.

youtube.title: Needs and Wants for Kids! Goods and Services | Grade 2 Social Studies | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Robo and Cat are getting ready for a sleep-out in the back garden, but Robo's shopping list only has fun things on it! At Bear's market stall we learn that needs are what we must have to live and stay healthy (food, water, shelter and warm clothing), and wants are nice extras. We sort things with the Can we live without it? test, use the Basket Test to tell goods (things you can hold) from services (work someone does for you), and help Robo choose with only 5 tokens: needs first, then one want. Ends with a quick-fire challenge and a quiz.

For second graders (C3 economics, grades K-2: needs and wants, goods and services, making choices).

Try at home with a grown-up: cut pictures from a shop flyer and sort them into NEED and WANT. Ask a grown-up to help with the scissors.

balloon
kite
cupcake
toy robot

A warm coat on a snowy day

do.text: Needs and Wants Market
Good morning! Welcome to my market stall.
Cat and I are having a sleep-out in a tent tonight, in the back garden.
Here is my shopping list. Balloon, kite, cupcake, a toy robot, more balloons!
Robo, what will we drink? What will keep us warm tonight?
Oh. I only wrote down fun things.
Let's learn the difference between needs and wants.
Needs are things we must have to live and stay healthy.
need
We need food. Food gives us energy to live and grow.
We need water. Our bodies need water every day.
We need clothing that keeps us warm and safe in the weather.
And we need shelter. Shelter keeps us safe and dry.
Food, water, clothing, shelter. Four needs!
Here's my test. Ask: can we live and stay healthy without it?
Can we live without it?
Water. Can we live without water?
No! So water is a need.
People can go weeks without food, but only a few days without water.
A balloon. Can we live without a balloon?
Yes, we can. So a balloon is a want.
want
Wants are nice extras. Fun, but we can live without them.
want = a nice extra
A balloon, a kite, a ball. Wants!
Are wants bad? Oh no, I love my wants!
Wants are fine! They're just not musts. We get needs first.
What about the cupcake? It's food, and food is a need.
Need or want?
Food is a need, but a cupcake is a treat. The treat is extra, so it's a want.
So a sandwich is a need, and a cupcake is a want. Got it!
Let's sort eight things. Green mat for needs, blue mat for wants.
I'll do it fast! Water, sandwich, apple on need.
Balloon on want. Kite on need!
Mittens on want. Socks on need, cupcake on want. Done!
Let me check. The kite is on need.
I need it! I really, really want it!
Could you live and stay healthy without a kite?
Yes. So the kite is a want.
And the mittens? We're sleeping outside on a cool night.
Mittens keep us warm, so tonight they are a need.
Clothes that keep us warm are needs. A fancy costume would be a want.
Five needs, three wants. Sorted!
At my stall, you can buy goods. Goods are things you can hold.
goods = things you can hold
Here's the Basket Test. If it fits in the basket, it's a good.
Can it go in the basket?
An apple and socks. Goods! Now I'll put in a bus ride.
Can a bus ride go in the basket?
No! You can't hold a ride. A bus ride is a service.
service
A service is work someone does for you.
services = work someone does for you
Like a haircut, or a check-up at the doctor's!
Oh! My knee is squeaky.
I can fix that. Oiling your knee is my service.
No more squeak! Here is one token for your work.
Robo paid for work, not for a thing. That's a service.
Need it to live?
Put it first!
Want it for fun?
Wait your turn!
Hug yourself for a need. Wave your hand for a want!
Prices today. Water 1 token, sandwich 2, socks 1.
Cupcake 1, balloon 1, and the kite costs 3 tokens.
I have 5 tokens. Will that be enough for everything?
Is 5 tokens enough?
No. Everything costs 9 tokens. So we must choose. Needs first!
not enough for everything
Water, 1 token.
4 left
Sandwich, 2 tokens.
2 left
Warm socks, 1 token.
1 left
Four tokens for needs. Five take away four leaves one token.
One token left. The balloon or the cupcake?
Not both. And the kite costs 3 tokens, too much today.
Hmm. It's hard to choose. I'll pick the balloon!
Choosing means giving something up. That's okay. We can save for the kite.
Fun fact! The word economy comes from a Greek word for running a home.

scenes.title: Challenge: Need, Want, Good or Service?

do.text: Quick-fire challenge! Is it a need or a want? A good or a service?
A warm coat on a snowy day.
A need, because it keeps us warm. And a good: you can hold it.
need + good
A video game.
A want. It's fun, but we can live without it. And it's a good.
want + good
A check-up at the doctor.
A service: the doctor does the work. And staying healthy is a need.
service + need
A skateboard.
A want, and a good. You can hold a skateboard.
want + good
A bus ride to school.
A service! Someone drives the bus for you.
service
Great sorting! You know needs, wants, goods and services.
Quiz time! Name two needs.
Food, water, clothing and shelter. Any two!
Is a balloon a need or a want?
A want!
want
Is a haircut a good or a service?
A service. It's work someone does for you.
service
I have 3 tokens. Water costs 1, a sandwich 2, a kite 3. What should I buy?
Water and a sandwich. Needs first! One plus two makes three.
1 + 2 = 3 tokens
Is it bad to have wants?
No! Wants are fine. We just choose needs first.
Let's remember. Needs keep us alive and healthy. Wants are nice extras.
Goods are things. Services are work. And choosing means giving something up.
Try it at home! Sort pictures from a shop flyer into needs and wants.
Ask a grown-up to help with scissors
Smart shopping! Here's a sticker for everyone.
Water to drink, warm socks, a tent, and one balloon. Checked!
Needs first, then a want. Good night, friends!
